annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "tap" on page 598 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea. During this Ricorso (The Return) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Gordon, John. Finnegans Blog (Tavern chapters). https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 598 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea. During this Ricorso (The Return) phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "wall" on page 598 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Ricorso (The Return) phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
